title: Quran Knowledge
description: General User → Beginner. Familiar Quran facts, broader basics and short everyday applications, all at Beginner level. No memorization of reference numbers is required.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: In which language was the Quran revealed?
questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed in Arabic.

questions.question: How many surahs are in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Quran contains 114 surahs.

questions.question: What is a surah?
questions.explanation: A surah is a chapter of the Quran.

references.label: Quran Foundation: chapter and verse reference documentation

questions.question: What is an ayah in the Quran?
questions.explanation: An ayah is a verse within a surah.

references.label: Quran Foundation: chapter and verse reference documentation

questions.question: Which surah comes first in the Quran's written order?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah opens the Quran's standard written order.

questions.question: Which surah comes last in the Quran's written order?
questions.explanation: An-Nas is the final surah in the standard written order.

questions.question: Which surah has the most ayahs?
questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah has 286 ayahs, more than any other surah.

questions.question: How many ayahs are in Al-Fatihah?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.

questions.question: How many ayahs are in Al-Kawthar?
questions.explanation: Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.

questions.question: What does the name Al-Fatihah mean?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah means The Opening.

questions.question: Which surah begins by declaring that Allah is One?
questions.explanation: Al-Ikhlas teaches Allah's oneness and uniqueness.

questions.question: What does An-Nas mean?
questions.explanation: An-Nas means people or humankind.

questions.question: What does Al-Falaq mean?
questions.explanation: Al-Falaq refers to daybreak.

questions.question: What does Al-Baqarah mean?
questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah means The Cow.

questions.question: Which month is associated with the Quran being revealed?
questions.explanation: The Quran names Ramadan as the month of its revelation.

questions.question: Which special night is linked with the Quran being sent down?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr names Laylat al-Qadr in connection with the Quran's descent.

questions.question: Which angel brought the Quran by Allah's permission?
questions.explanation: Jibril brought the revelation to the Prophet's heart.

questions.question: To which prophet was the Quran revealed?
questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

questions.question: What does the Quran offer people?

options.text: Permission to ignore right and wrong

questions.explanation: The Quran describes itself as guidance.

questions.question: Ayat al-Kursi is part of which surah?
questions.explanation: Ayat al-Kursi is an ayah in Al-Baqarah.

questions.question: Which prophet was told to build an ark?
questions.explanation: The Quran describes Allah instructing Nuh to build the ark.

questions.question: Which prophet's story includes being swallowed by a great fish?
questions.explanation: The Quran tells this part of Yunus's story.

questions.question: Which prophet was sent with Harun to Pharaoh?
questions.explanation: Allah instructed Musa and Harun to go to Pharaoh.

questions.question: Which prophet told his father about a dream of eleven stars, the sun and the moon?
questions.explanation: Yusuf describes this dream to his father in Surah Yusuf.

questions.question: Which woman has a Quran surah named after her?
questions.explanation: Surah Maryam is named after Maryam, the mother of Isa.

questions.question: Which surah tells the story of the Companions of the Cave?
questions.explanation: The story appears in Surah Al-Kahf, whose name means The Cave.

questions.question: In the Quran, Luqman gives advice to which family member?
questions.explanation: The Quran records Luqman's advice to his son.

questions.question: Who raised the foundations of the Kabah with Ibrahim?
questions.explanation: The Quran names Ibrahim and Ismail together in raising the House's foundations.

questions.question: How does the Quran teach us to speak to parents?
questions.explanation: The Quran commands honourable speech and kindness toward parents.

questions.question: Does the Quran require fairness toward people we dislike?
questions.explanation: Hatred must not lead people away from justice.

questions.question: What kind of speech does the Quran instruct believers to use?

options.text: Claims made without concern for truth

questions.explanation: The Quran calls believers to speak rightly and truthfully.

questions.question: What behaviour toward people in need does Surah Al-Maun criticize?

options.text: Failing to encourage feeding the poor

questions.explanation: The surah criticizes harshness toward the orphan and neglect of feeding the poor.

questions.question: What does the Quran tell people who have sinned not to lose hope in?
questions.explanation: Allah calls people not to despair of His mercy and to return to Him.

questions.question: What response to blessings does the Quran encourage?
questions.explanation: The Quran encourages gratitude for Allah's blessings.

questions.question: What does the Quran tell believers to hold firmly to together?
questions.explanation: The Quran calls believers to hold firmly together to Allah's rope and avoid division.

questions.question: Which teaching about religion is found in the Quran?

options.text: There is no compulsion in religion.

questions.explanation: The Quran states that there is no compulsion in religion.

questions.question: In Al-Falaq, whose protection do we seek?
questions.explanation: Al-Falaq teaches seeking refuge with Allah, the Lord of daybreak.

questions.question: In Al-Fatihah, whom do we worship and ask for help?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah declares worship of Allah and seeking His help.

questions.question: Which request for parents appears in the Quran?

options.text: Ask that no one ever advises them.
Ask to be free from all kindness to them.
Ask Allah to have mercy on them.
Ask for wealth instead of any care for them.

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches a dua asking Allah's mercy for parents.

questions.question: What reassurance appears in Surah Ash-Sharh?

options.text: No believer will ever have a difficult day.
Every problem must end within one hour.

questions.explanation: The surah gives hope by affirming ease with hardship.

questions.question: You are learning to recite. Which approach is better?

options.text: Read carefully rather than rush past the words.
Race through even if words become unclear.
Change words to fit a tune.
Skip any word you find difficult.

questions.explanation: The Quran instructs measured recitation.

questions.question: You have read a short surah. What can help you learn from it?

options.text: Think about its meaning and lesson.
Assume reading its title is enough.
Treat its message as unrelated to life.

questions.explanation: The Quran calls people to reflect on its verses.

questions.question: You do not understand Arabic yet. What can help you understand a passage?

options.text: Invent a meaning from its sound.
Read a reliable translation of its meaning.

questions.explanation: Understanding matters. A reliable translation can help a learner access the meaning while continuing to learn.

questions.question: Reciting is difficult for you. What is a helpful next step?

options.text: Stop because only fluent readers matter.

questions.explanation: The Prophet gave encouragement to a reader who struggles with recitation.

questions.question: You can read a short surah correctly and someone wants to learn it. What is helpful?

options.text: Invent words to make it easier.
Tell them learning has no value.

questions.explanation: The Prophet praised learning the Quran and teaching it.

questions.question: You are about to recite the Quran. What does it teach you to seek?
questions.explanation: The Quran instructs seeking refuge in Allah when reciting.

questions.question: A parent needs help while you are tired. Which response reflects the Quran's teaching?

options.text: Use your tiredness to justify contempt.
Answer respectfully and help as you are able.
Humiliate them in front of others.

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches respectful speech and mercy toward parents.

questions.question: You must judge a disagreement involving someone you dislike. What should guide you?
questions.explanation: The Quran says hostility must not lead to injustice.

questions.question: You receive an unverified accusation about someone. What should you do before spreading it?

options.text: Forward it because it is dramatic.
Add details to make it convincing.
Assume many shares prove it true.

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against harming people through unchecked reports.

questions.question: Friends laugh at someone and ask you to join. Which choice fits the Quran?

options.text: Join so they will like you.
Film the person for more laughs.

questions.explanation: The Quran forbids ridiculing people and offensive name-calling.

questions.question: You want to read someone's private messages just out of curiosity. What Quranic teaching matters?

options.text: Privacy matters only for famous people.

questions.explanation: The Quran prohibits spying on one another.

questions.question: You give someone help. How should you treat them afterward?

options.text: Keep reminding them they owe you praise.
Use the gift to justify insults.

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against spoiling charity with reminders and hurt.

questions.question: You receive a blessing. Which response follows Quranic teaching?

options.text: Boast that you need no help from anyone.

questions.explanation: The Quran encourages gratitude and righteous use of blessings.

questions.question: You realize you have done wrong. What does the Quran encourage?

options.text: Give up all hope of mercy.
Return to Allah and seek forgiveness.
Keep doing it because change is pointless.

questions.explanation: The Quran offers hope in Allah's mercy and calls people to return to Him.

questions.question: You can offer only a small kindness today. Should you dismiss it as worthless?

options.text: No, even a small good deed matters.
Yes, unless it makes you famous.

questions.explanation: The Quran says even an atom's weight of good will be seen.

questions.question: Someone leaves an item with you for safekeeping. What should you do?

options.text: Keep it because you like it.
Return it to its rightful owner.

questions.explanation: The Quran commands returning trusts to their rightful owners.

questions.question: You make a promise. How should you treat it?

options.text: As important only if recorded on video
As a reason to mislead others

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches fulfilling commitments and accountability for them.

questions.question: You are deciding how to spend. Which approach does the Quran praise?
questions.explanation: The Quran describes a balanced course between extravagance and miserliness.

questions.question: Someone speaks harshly to you. Which response is encouraged by Quranic teaching?

options.text: Assume anger makes every response right.

questions.explanation: The Quran encourages responding to evil with what is better.

questions.question: You are starting a lesson. Which Quranic dua fits learning?

options.text: Make me need no learning ever again.
Make every guess of mine correct.
Let me avoid all questions forever.
My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches asking Allah for increased knowledge.
